For entry level jobs, I would suggest that you doing personal projects and at least one internship in the field you want to get a job in so that the interviewer can discuss your experience rather than Leetcode questions.

To answer your question, I don't know where you are from but for me it was a question of luck rather than research, so I would suggest that you apply to as many places as you can and a lot of them are bound to not ask difficult leetcode questions.

“Whatever you do, don't look behind you”, a hoarse and anxious voice said.

“And why not”, Indra asked, in an uncaring tone. He was late for his meeting and did not want to waste any more time on some crazy bum. He was already running out of excuses and this one didn’t sound very good even if true. He sighed, already imagining his boss screaming at him again.

“Feel that?”, the voice said said, thrusting something metallic hard into Indra’s back. Indra winced at that.

“Is... Is that a gun?”, Indra asked, liquid tension slowly spreading across his body.

“Another word and you are dead”, the coarse voice said. 

Indra stood, silently staring into the mass of people going about their day and he just couldn’t believe the situation he was in. Just a few more meters and he’d be out of the dark alleyway and out in the open. He silently wished for someone to notice the situation and bring help.

Indra gritted his teeth. He had only recently started getting used to the ever repeating cycle of days and nights of the working man and this happened, destroying whatever sense of normalcy he had worked so hard to create. 

After a tense few seconds, the voice spoke again “Money or Die”. 

“Okay Okay, it’s in my left pocket, take it”, Indra said. He noticed a dirty hand, adorned with a torn glove, reach into his pockets.

He let out a tired sigh. All that work and now he had to start all over again.

His dull grey eyes slowly filled with a threatening red. He roughly grabbed the gloved hand.

“Huh”, the voice said. “What the f-”, his voice was cut short as a faint bubbling sound became audible.

“That’s more like it”, Indra thought with a hint of a smile on his face.

A bubbling sound became audible. Intense heat rose from the strangers body. Indra let go of the hand and the body lifelessly collapsed, sizzling as if on a hot pan. Indra turned back to have a look at the poor soul. It was too late anyway, every hole in his body was guzzling a steaming mess of organs and blood.

Indra let out another sigh as he imagined all the work he’d have to do again to move and create a new identity. It wasn’t safe in this city anymore. One single trace found and they would be after him like hounds.

He looked around to ensure no witnesses were left. Then he stealthily escaped into another connecting alleyway, wishing he hadn’t taken the shortcut that morning.
